q: Can a CloudWatch Logs export task write to another account's S3 bucket or an Object Lock bucket?
v: same account or a different account
S3 Object Lock enabled with a retention period
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/S3Export
You can export to an S3 bucket in the same account or a different account.
docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/S3Export
Export log data to S3 buckets that have S3 Object Lock enabled with a retention period

claim: You can keep exported log files in your S3 bucket and define Amazon S3 lifecycle rules to archive or delete them automatically.
q: How do you archive or expire exported CloudWatch log files?
v: archive or delete exported files automatically
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/S3Export
You can store the exported files in your S3 bucket and define Amazon S3 lifecycle rules to archive or delete exported files automatically.

claim: CloudWatch Logs Insights cannot access log events with timestamps that pre-date the creation time of the log group.
q: Can Logs Insights query events older than the log group's creation time?
v: pre-date the creation time of the log group
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData
CloudWatch Logs Insights can't access log events with timestamps that pre-date the creation time of the log group.

claim: In a monitoring account set up for CloudWatch cross-account observability, you can run CloudWatch Logs Insights queries on log groups in the linked source accounts, including one query across log groups in different accounts.
q: Can one Logs Insights query cover log groups from several accounts?
v: queries multiple log groups located in different accounts
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData

If you are signed in to an account set up as a monitoring account in CloudWatch cross-account observability, you can run CloudWatch Logs Insights queries on log groups in source accounts linked to this monitoring account. You can run a query that queries multiple log groups located in different accounts.

claim: CloudWatch Logs Live Tail lets you troubleshoot incidents by viewing a streaming list of new log events as they are ingested, and you can view, filter and highlight them in near real time.
q: Which CloudWatch Logs feature shows new log events as they arrive?
v: streaming list of new log events
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CloudWatchLogs_LiveTail

CloudWatch Logs Live Tail helps you quickly troubleshoot incidents by viewing a streaming list of new log events as they are ingested. You can view, filter, and highlight ingested logs in near real time, helping you to detect and resolve issues quickly.

claim: Live Tail sessions incur costs by session usage time, per minute.
q: How is CloudWatch Logs Live Tail charged?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CloudWatchLogs_LiveTail
Live Tail sessions incur costs by session usage time, per minute.

claim: A log anomaly detector scans the log events ingested into a log group and finds anomalies automatically, using machine learning and pattern recognition to establish baselines of typical log content.
q: How does CloudWatch Logs find unusual log patterns automatically?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/LogsAnomalyDetection

A log anomaly detector scans the log events ingested into a log group and finds anomalies in the log data automatically. Anomaly detection uses machine-learning and pattern recognition to establish baselines of typical log content.

claim: Logs transformation and enrichment lets you normalize your logs into a consistent, context-rich format at the time of ingestion into CloudWatch Logs.
q: Can CloudWatch Logs reshape log events as they are ingested?
v: at the time of ingestion into CloudWatch Logs
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CloudWatch-Logs-Transformation
With logs transformation and enrichment, you can normalize all your logs in a consistent and context-rich format at the time of ingestion into CloudWatch Logs.

claim: Log Analytics is a unified console experience in CloudWatch Logs that brings together CloudWatch Logs Insights, Live Tail and Contributor Insights, and it is the default experience for analyzing logs in the CloudWatch Logs console.
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/LogAnalytics

Log Analytics is a unified console experience in Amazon CloudWatch Logs that brings together log analysis capabilities in one place. You can query and analyze log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights, stream logs in real time with Live Tail, and identify your top contributors with CloudWatch Contributor Insights. Log Analytics is the default experience for analyzing logs in the CloudWatch Logs console.

claim: Many AWS services publish logs only to CloudWatch Logs, while others use vended log delivery to send logs directly to Amazon S3 or Amazon Data Firehose.
q: Where can AWS services deliver their vended logs?
v: publish logs only to CloudWatch Logs
vended log delivery to send logs directly
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AWS-logs-and-resource-policy
Many services publish logs only to CloudWatch Logs, but others use vended log delivery to send logs directly to Amazon Simple Storage Service or Amazon Data Firehose.

claim: Even when a service publishes logs directly to Amazon S3 or Firehose, CloudWatch delivery charges apply.
q: Are vended logs sent directly to S3 or Firehose free of CloudWatch charges?
v: publish logs directly to Amazon S3 or Firehose
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AWS-logs-and-resource-policy
Even when you publish logs directly to Amazon S3 or Firehose, CloudWatch delivery charges apply.

claim: If a log group has no resource policy and the user setting up logging has the needed logs permissions, AWS automatically creates the resource policy that lets the service write logs when you begin sending the logs to CloudWatch Logs.
q: Who creates the log group resource policy for vended logs?
v: AWS automatically creates the following policy
log group currently does not have a resource policy
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AWS-logs-infrastructure-CWL

If the log group currently does not have a resource policy, and the user setting up the logging has the `logs:PutResourcePolicy`, `logs:DescribeResourcePolicies`, and `logs:DescribeLogGroups` permissions for the log group, then AWS automatically creates the following policy for it when you begin sending the logs to CloudWatch Logs.
